answer: No, they do not impose the same minimum investment threshold. The original definition requires an investment of "not less than seventy crore rupees" while the November 2025-amended definition requires an investment of "not less than twenty-five crore rupees".

citations.quote: Regulation 2(1)(pa) (before November 2025 amendment): 'large value fund for accredited investors' means an Alternative Investment Fund or scheme of an Alternative Investment Fund in which each investor (other than the Manager, Sponsor, employees or directors of the Alternative Investment Fund or employees or directors of the Manager) is an accredited investor and invests not less than seventy crore rupees.

Regulation 2(1)(pa) (as amended w.e.f. 19-11-2025): 'large value fund for accredited investors' means an Alternative Investment Fund or scheme of an Alternative Investment Fund in which each investor (other than the Manager, Sponsor, employees or directors of the Alternative Investment Fund or employees or directors of the Manager) is an accredited investor and invests not less than twenty-five crore rupees.

Under the original SEBI (Issue and Listing of Debt Securities by Municipalities) Regulations 2015, the trust deed had to be executed within three months of the closure of the issue. With the issue closing on 1 January 2018, the latest date for execution was 1 April 2018 (1 January 2018 + 3 months).

answer: As of 2020-01-01, the evidence for the specific dual threshold rule under Regulation 13(e) refers to a 2025 amendment version or general text without showing the active 2020 text for Regulation 13(e), but the text provided states: individuals registered as investment advisers whose number of clients exceed three hundred at any point of time or the fee collected during the financial year exceeds three crore rupees, whichever is earlier shall — (i) immediately intimate the Administration and Supervisory Body and initiate the process of transition from individual to non-individual investment adviser; and (ii) apply for grant of in-principle approval for registration as non-individual investment adviser within 3 months from the date on which the threshold is reached.

answer: As of 2020-01-01, no scheme of the Alternative Investment Fund shall have more than one thousand investors. All investors, including accredited investors, were counted toward this limit.

citations.quote: No scheme of the Alternative Investment Fund shall have more than one thousand investors.
Prior to this amendment, all investors including accredited investors were counted toward the 1,000 cap.

answer: As of 2020-01-01, the minimum eligibility criteria for a credit rating agency applicant under SEBI (CRA) Regulations, 1999 are: (a) the applicant must be set up and registered as a company under the Companies Act, 2013; (b) the applicant must have, in its Memorandum of Association, specified rating activity as one of its main objects; and (c) the applicant must have a minimum net worth of rupees twenty five crore.

citations.quote: Regulation 5(a)–(c): The Board shall not consider an application unless — (a) the applicant is set up and registered as a company under the Companies Act, 2013; (b) the applicant has, in its Memorandum of Association, specified rating activity as one of its main objects; (c) the applicant has a minimum net worth of rupees twenty five crore.
